title: Inspect grounding, distortion and control-power loops
lead: Low resistance, low distortion and a nominal battery voltage each answer only a narrowly defined question. This lesson turns those single numbers into explicit boundaries. Follow the ground current, compare harmonic denominators, and include the return conductor in the trip circuit before drawing any conclusion about service.
objectives: Distinguish ground-potential rise from touch/step assessment.
Calculate THD and TDD using different denominators.
Evaluate a complete DC loop and explain frequency-change consequences.

sections.title: Grounding has several functions
sections.body: Protective bonding, source-neutral grounding, lightning protection and signal/EMC interfaces are related but not interchangeable. In the deliberately simplified resistive model, 2 kA entering a 0.5 Ω grounding system gives 1,000 V ground-potential rise. It does not automatically give the voltage across a person. Soil structure, geometry, current distribution, bonding, surface layer, duration and the applicable criterion remain necessary for a safety assessment.

sections.title: Choose the correct distortion denominator
sections.body: THD uses aggregate harmonic RMS current divided by fundamental RMS current. TDD uses the same numerator divided by a declared reference maximum-demand current. With 30 A harmonics, 100 A fundamental and 300 A reference, THD is 30% and TDD is 10%. Those different percentages describe the same numerator. A generic five-percent statement without a metric, operating state and boundary is not a universal conformity rule.

sections.title: Close the return path and preserve physical duty
sections.body: A two-wire DC route has both outgoing and return conductors. At 10 A, one-way length 100 m and resistance 0.003 Ω/m, the conductor drop is 6 V before contacts and other elements. The minimum loaded source voltage and receiving coil requirement still govern. Frequency changes are also physical changes: at unchanged voltage, 60-to-50 Hz increases ideal transformer flux by 20%; rotating-equipment affinity relations have their own stated assumptions.

challenge.question: What changes if the fundamental current falls while harmonics and reference demand stay fixed?
challenge.answer: THD rises to 60%; TDD stays at 10%. This demonstrates denominator sensitivity, not a new measured harmonic event.
